source_text:
Also I was thinking for the proforma we could use terms from the Enclosed CJK Letters and Months Unicode block (U+3200 to U+32FF) and the Enclosed Ideographic Supplement block (U+1F200 to U+1F2FF).  Regarding the "cheaper" training system, let's not try to make it cheaper but let's ensure that the segements and intents are well-processed.  I'd like it to feed both the pattern graph and the 小象 system.  We can use zai, kimi, and Sonnet for tagging, they are all "cheap enough" and we will likely get some varied reads (which is good, in my opinion).

Examples of potential characters to use in your proforma presentation:
• ㊭ U+32AD – Circled Ideograph Enterprise (企)
• ㊮ U+32AE – Circled Ideograph Resource (資)
• ㊯ U+32AF – Circled Ideograph Alliance (協)
• ㊰ U+32B0 – Circled Ideograph Night (夜)
• ㊬ U+32AC – Circled Ideograph Supervise (監)

reply_text:
㊥ Gist: I like the enclosed characters for the proforma and have drafted a mapping below. On tagging, understood: the full contract on every turn, with Zai, Kimi and Sonnet all reading.

㊣ Approve (enclosed characters as labels): A single codepoint at the start of a paragraph is easier to parse than a word like "Report:", which also turns up in ordinary prose. I am using them in this reply as a trial.

㊭ Propose (a mapping, drawn from the two blocks you named):

| Intent | Mark | Character's sense |
|---|---|---|
| gist | ㊥ | 中, middle |
| propose | ㊭ | 企, plan |
| approve | ㊣ | 正, correct |
| disagree | 🈚 | 無, not |
| qualify | ㊟ | 注, note |
| explain | 🈖 | 解, explain |
| clarify | 🈯 | 指, point at |
| report | ㊢ | 写, record |
| report-problem | ㊩ | 医, diagnosis |
| verify | ㊬ | 監, inspect |
| constrain | 🈲 | 禁, prohibit |
| ask-action | 🈸 | 申, request |
| delegate | ㊯ | 協, cooperate |
| prioritize | ㊝ | 優, priority |
| collect | ㊮ | 資, resources |
| extend | 🈕 | 多, more |
| continue | 🈰 | 走, run |
| defer | 🈝 | 後, after |
| redirect | 🈘 | 交, cross over |
| explore | ㊫ | 学, study |
| retract | 🈹 | 割, cut |
| withdraw | 🈡 | 終, end |
| unresolved | 🈳 | 空, empty |

Four of your five examples are in it (㊭, ㊮, ㊯, ㊬); ㊰ 夜 is unassigned.

㊟ Qualify (rendering): The second block, 🈚 🈖 🈲 and the rest, is in the supplementary plane. Many terminal fonts draw those as wide emoji or as blanks. I asked your Emacs which font it would use for four of these and got no answer, which is expected in a terminal frame, so I cannot tell how they look to you. If any show as boxes, I can redraw the table from the first block alone, which has 49 circled ideographs.

㊟ Qualify (speech): Only the Gist paragraph is read aloud, so the marks elsewhere cost nothing. I do not know what the voice does with ㊥ at the start of the Gist; if it reads it oddly, the Gist could keep the plain word.

㊢ Report (backfill chunk 1): zai-2 is still running and has published 6 of the 10 turns in about 20 minutes, so roughly three minutes a record under the full contract. I will check the chunk when the park fires.

㊭ Propose (running the backfill with mixed readers):
1. A plain loop that sends ten turns a job, runs the mechanical check on each chunk, and only then sends the next.
2. Seats rotate between Zai, Kimi and 象-sonnet, with the reader recorded on every reading, as it already is.
3. One turn in ten goes to two different readers. That gives a measured agreement rate between readers, which tells 小象's training how noisy the labels are.
4. The closed label list is enforced at publish time, so new readings do not repeat the 634-label spread of the older batches.

🈸 Ask-action (two confirmations):
- Shall I build that loop once chunk 1 passes its check? At three minutes a record, the 9,300 remaining turns are about 470 seat-hours, so several seats for some days.
- Is the mapping above acceptable as a first version, or would you rather choose the characters yourself?
